seeds.title: Trailing newline accepted by rows 5 to 8
seeds.detail: parse('sdlc/{name}','sdlc/S-001\n') gives kind slice, and the same for state, attempt and verify tails. Python `$` matches before a final newline. Same open item as S-007.

seeds.title: Non-ASCII digits accepted by \d
seeds.detail: sdlc/state-٢٠٢٦١٠٠٨١٠١٥٠٠ gives kind state; sdlc/S-001-attempt-٣ gives kind attempt; sdlc/S-001-v٠-cli-٠ gives kind verify. int() converts them, so n becomes 3.

seeds.title: Attempt and verify rows accept any id text
seeds.detail: Rows 6 and 7 use (.+) for id. sdlc/--flag-attempt-1 and a tail with a NUL or a lone surrogate before -attempt-1 give kind attempt with that text as id. Callers that pass id to a shell or git must treat it as untrusted.

seeds.title: Huge digit runs give unbounded integers
seeds.detail: A 5000-digit round, part or n parses to a Python int, because set_int_max_str_digits(0) removes the limit. Output JSON holds the full integer.

seeds.title: Public names beyond the spec API
seeds.detail: The module exports PARSE_ROWS and INTEGER_PARTS as public names. The spec lists neither.

seeds.title: Shared run worktree was edited during verification
seeds.detail: At the start of the round, the working copy of skills/sdlc/branches.py in the run worktree held an uncommitted change that removed parse. It was restored later. This agent tested a separate worktree on commit d29cba7. A parallel mutation check probably caused it.

seeds.title: One property batch timed out once
seeds.detail: One run of 3000 calls hit the 120 s spawn limit in the first attempt. Ten later runs of the same size took under 100 ms each, and 47 seeds gave no failure. The cause was probably machine load. The run is inconclusive, not a defect.
